subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should agent- or plugin-initiated configuration changes be prohibited by default at the CLI/exec boundary, or allowed only through an explicitly approved and auditable automation contract?
rationale: The reported behavior crosses persisted operator configuration, agent host-exec authority, sandbox posture, and scheduled-job availability; source-level confirmation alone cannot choose the intended authority model.

options.title: Block unattended config writes
options.body: Require explicit operator approval for configuration mutation originating from agent or plugin execution, then preserve advisory-only diagnostics.

options.title: Define an audited automation contract
options.body: Allow narrowly scoped automated writes only through a named, permissioned, and auditable subsystem with clear migration and rollback behavior.

recommendation.title: Block unattended config writes
recommendation.body: Require explicit operator approval for configuration mutation originating from agent or plugin execution, then preserve advisory-only diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The only concrete related implementation proposal concerns the agent-visible sandbox diagnostic path, though broader ownership still needs repository-history confirmation.
